newsitem.title: FRANCE: EMU without Italy unimaginable - BoF's Marchelli.
newsitem.headline: EMU without Italy unimaginable - BoF's Marchelli.

text.p: It would be unimaginable to launch European Economic and Monetary Union without Italy, while Spain and Portugal should also be in from the start, Bank of France council member Paul Marchelli said on Friday.

Marchelli, known for his controversial views, also told Reuters that he believed Germany wanted an excessively strong euro and if a broad-based EMU resulted in a weaker euro this would be a good thing for employment in Europe.

"The Germans, who want a strong euro, in my opinion too strong a euro, tend to reject the southern countries," he said. "They fear that the euro will not be strong enough. That is the only problem of the Italians."
"If the base for EMU is wide and if the currency is less strong than (Bundesbank President Hans) Tietmeyer hopes, that would be an excellent thing," he added.
The construction of Europe must be based on a balance between north and south.
"I cannot imagine the euro without Italy. It is impossible. It is like having Paris without the Eiffel Tower. It is ridiculous," he added. "We must have Italy, Spain and Portugal."
